I'm try to put together a little "show and tell" for regression for some people.  However, the output must be in Word.  Don't ask, please.

Anyhow, I'm using knitr to produce a nice Markdown file.  Then I'm using pandoc to transfer over to Word.  But the summary output from the linear regression does not appear.

I will attach what I have (hope that's ok) and any suggestions would be much appreciated.  I've tried all kinds of things.

Thanks,
Erin

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Markdown to Word via pandoc printing a linear regression summary table
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Markdown to Word via pandoc printing a linear regression summary table
messages.body_plain:
You have neither the {r} syntax to signal knitr that this is executable nor the result='as.is <http://as.is>' chunk option to tell knitr to pass through the output from the xtable object into the knitr output for handling downstream. Unfortunately, you don't seem to be including latex or html in your tool chain, so xtable is unlikely to work for you either. The knitr "kable" function might help.

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Markdown to Word via pandoc printing a linear regression summary table
messages.body_plain:
Look at the pander package, it has tools for producing markdown syntax from many standard R outputs.  It can be used with knitr (and the type asis) or it can also feed directly to markdown documents and convert them to word.  I have used it with and without knitr for clients who insist on having the results in Word (some insist on Word output even after my attempted jokes about Word as a word processor treating the output like a food processor treats food).

messages.subject: Re: Code with different colors
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I don't believe there is anyway to achieve that in knitr/markdown directly.

Probably the most straight-forward way would be to post-process the output and wrap each section you want to highlight in a <div> block and assign it a CSS class with the settings you would like to use.

Best,
Keith

messages.subject: Re: Hmisc summary.formula in html markdown
messages.body_plain:
I am updating this old post with something that may be of assistance.

Try the new package moonBook <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/moonBook/vignettes/moonBook.html>, this gives you a similar table to that using summary.formula, but has better support for html output. It can also be used in companion with ztable <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ztable/vignettes/ztable.html> by the same author wich has excellent table options and supports markdown.

If you have a large dataset, I recommend the development version of the moonBook package, which has recently been updated to better support this.

Best regards,
Tormod

messages.subject: How can I display (not just read data from) a Google Spreadsheet in a Chunk? (Spreadsheet has merged cells)
messages.subject_clean: How can I display (not just read data from) a Google Spreadsheet in a Chunk? (Spreadsheet has merged cells)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

How can I visually display a Google Spreadsheet in a chunk? I don't just want to read the data in the chunk, I actually want to visually display the spreadsheet. In other words, the spreadsheet is part of the "narrative" as well as the source code. Either a Latex/pdf or a Markdown/html solution is fine with me. Converting it to .csv is not a solution for me, because my spreadsheet has merged cells (which my R code can parse correctly).

Probably any solution that can display a spreadsheet with merged cells, but still treat it as source code will work for me. I do not want to break the "knit/weave" paradigm.

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Markdown to PDF
messages.body_plain:
What you're seeing in your browser is a function of HTML + CSS + any quirks of your browser's rendering engine.

To get a PDF which looks the same, your best bet is probably to use the browser's save to PDF feature.
